common_name: ColorBlaze Lime Time Coleus (Bright Chartreuse Sun-Tolerant Coleus)

planting.note: Plant container starts in spring after the last frost in full sun to full shade; Lime Time, part of the ColorBlaze series, holds its bright chartreuse color across an unusually wide range of light exposures.

directions: Plant container starts in spring after the last frost in a bed or large pot that gets anything from full sun to full shade, since Lime Time is bred to hold its color and vigor across that entire range without bleaching or stretching. Part of the ColorBlaze series, it produces simple, unmarked chartreuse-lime leaves on a tall, well-branched, mounding plant that reads as a solid block of glowing color from a distance, making it an effective bright foil for darker-leaved companions like 'ColorBlaze Dark Star' or purple-leaved annuals. Its size and vigor suit it to landscape mass plantings, large mixed containers, and anywhere a strong chartreuse accent is needed through summer and into fall. Pinch off flower spikes as they form and pinch growing tips periodically to keep the plant dense rather than lanky.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, pressing the fine seed onto the mix surface since light aids germination; Pineapple Surprise tolerates full sun far better than older seed coleus strains.

directions: Start the fine seed indoors on the surface of moist mix, since it needs light to germinate, then transplant into full sun or partial shade after the last frost. Premium Sun Pineapple Surprise bears golden-yellow leaves splashed with maroon markings radiating from the center vein, on a compact, uniformly mounded plant bred from seed to perform reliably from a young age without the fading some older gold-toned coleus show in strong sun. Pinch the growing tips and remove flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant bushy and focused on foliage color. Its compact size and bright gold tone make it a dependable choice for edging, mass bedding, and mixed containers.

common_name: Kong Scarlet Coleus (Giant-Leaved Scarlet-and-Burgundy Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant container plants after the last frost in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kong Scarlet, bred by Sakata and marketed by Ball Horticultural, is among the largest-leaved coleus available and needs protection from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and keep soil consistently moist, since the Kong series' enormous leaves wilt quickly in dry conditions. Kong Scarlet is part of the Kong coleus series bred for exceptionally large leaves, with bright scarlet centers framed by dark burgundy edging and a light green outer margin, giving each leaf several distinct bands of color. Its huge foliage and compact-for-its-size habit make a dramatic statement massed in shaded beds or as a specimen in a large container, pairing well with ferns, hostas, and other big-leaved shade perennials. Pinch flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into leaf growth, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a fuller, bushier habit.
